To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the naturalness of an image can be measured by a single parameter, namely the contrast ratio, and that this parameter is related to the contrast sensitivity function of the human visual system.
the naturalness of a high dynamic range image is the weighted linear combination of the image's attributes: contrast, colorfulness, saturation, sharpness, and detail.
the naturalness of reproduced images can be measured by the following attributes, in the following order of importance: contrast, colorfulness, and saturation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a thorough analysis of the problem of visualizing the high dynamic range images, which we believe is a necessary prerequisite for the further progress in the field.
a thorough understanding of high dynamic range images in order to enable the development of a high-quality visualization pipeline.
the development of a quality model that will enable the design and implementation of high quality tone mapping operators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the naturalness of a tone mapped image can be predicted from a set of image attributes.
a tone mapping operator is good if it is able to preserve naturalness of an image, which is defined as a set of objective and subjective attributes.
the quality of the image is determined by its attributes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a new quality measure which is well founded on the subjective perception of high dynamic range images, and we have shown its validity in psychophysical testing.
the naturalness of a high dynamic range image depends on a number of image attributes which can be measured and compared.
we provide a well-founded basis for future research in the field of tone mapping.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the naturalness measure, which we have defined, is a valid quality measure.
the quality of a reproduced high dynamic range image is determined by its naturalness, which is a function of its contrast, color saturation, and noise.
we provide a framework for the comparison of tone mapping operators.
